requested_checks.question: Discover the backend metric set over 2026-10-01T11:45:00Z-2026-10-01T13:00:00Z with empty metric_names, then compare pool_active, max_pool_size and pool_waiters against cpu_utilization, memory_utilization and request_latency_ms to determine whether the pool is pinned while local resources stay flat or local resources saturate.
requested_checks.reason: Empty metric_names surfaces the real backend metric set, and pool-versus-resource behavior on one shared timeline is the discriminator between pool misconfiguration and local saturation that the current records cannot settle.
requested_checks.expected_discriminator: pool_waiters elevated with pool_active at max_pool_size and flat cpu_utilization/memory_utilization indicates pool misconfiguration, whereas rising cpu_utilization/memory_utilization with latency indicates local resource saturation.

requested_checks.question: Report postgres connection and session health over 2026-10-01T11:45:00Z-2026-10-01T13:00:00Z, including active sessions, connection counts against limits, lock waits and slow queries, to test whether backend pool waiting is caused by postgres-side connection exhaustion rather than backend-local pool sizing.
requested_checks.reason: backend depends on postgres per the topology record, so a concrete competing cause for elevated backend pool_waiters is postgres-side connection exhaustion; this check supplies the database-side chronology needed to separate it from a backend pool configuration regression.
requested_checks.expected_discriminator: active sessions and connection counts at or near the postgres limit with lock waits or slow queries indicate postgres connection exhaustion, whereas a healthy postgres session count with backend pool_waiters still elevated points back to backend pool configuration.
